newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica, PNC Bank net income rise on quarter.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica, PNC Bank net income rise on quarter.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp. said Wednesday that its profits grew by 11 percent in the second quarter, while PNC Bank Corp. reported net income rose 4 percent.
San Francisco-based BankAmerica, the nation's third largest bank, reported net income climbed to $799 million during the quarter, compared with $723 million in the same period a year ago.
Non-interest net income rose 9 percent to $122 million. The growth included an $84 million increase in fees and commissions, primarily due to higher loan-servicing fees.
Earnings per share rose to $1.07 from 92 cents a share a year ago. The per-share results reflect a two-for-one stock split on June 2.
The results topped analysts' average forecast of $1.04 per share, according to the First Call service. BankAmerica's stock was up $1.94 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday, at $68.56 a share.

At Pittsburgh-based PNC Bank, net income rose to $259 million vs. $248 million in the second quarter of 1996. Earnings per share rose to 81 cents, from 72 cents a share a year ago, matching analysts' expectations.
Non-interest income in the second quarter shot up 29 percent, to $433.4 million, from $336.6 million a year ago, boosted by strong growth in fee-based businesses.
Fee-based revenue rose 21 percent, led by gains in its asset management, private banking, treasury management and capital markets sectors, the company said.

"These businesses are among the growth opportunities we have been pursuing for some time that are now making a more meaningful contribution to our financial performance," PNC Bank Chairman Thomas O'Brien said in a statement.
PNC said asset management fees increased $22 million, or 17 percent, primarily due to higher investment advisory, private banking and mutual fund servicing revenue.

Managed assets rose to about $122 billion at the end of the quarter, from $104 billion a year ago. Service fees increased $43 million, or 33 percent, primarily from growth in credit card, deposit and treasury management services and capital markets fee income, the company said.
PNC was trading 87.5 cents higher at $43.31 a share on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
